units.text: EXT. BACKYARD - CHICKEN COOP - AFTERNOON
A leafy suburban yard in late summer.
A hand-built chicken coop painted lemon yellow, tin-roofed, with a crooked sign: "THE HEN HOUSE."
Paper streamers sag from a clothesline.
A card table holds a half-eaten cake.
BEATRIX "BEA" LOMBARDI (8, gap-toothed, tiara over frizzy curls) squats in front of the coop, holding a speckled hen in both arms like a baby.
Her older brother THEO LOMBARDI (12, headphones around his neck, deliberately bored) leans against the fence.
Their mother, JUNE LOMBARDI (40s, apron, flour on her cheek), carries out a tray of lemonade.
Bea, put Penelope down. She's not a doll.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: She likes it.
units.name: BEA

units.text: She's literally about to peck your eye.
units.name: THEO

units.text: She is not!
units.name: BEA

units.text: The hen flaps.
Bea squeals and drops her.
Penelope lands in the dirt, ruffles, struts away with great dignity.
Theo, be nice. It's her birthday.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: I am nice. I came outside.
units.name: THEO

units.text: That's the minimum, honey.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: The gate clicks.
A tall man in a straw hat strides in, a wrapped box under one arm.
GRANDPA OSWALDO (70s, big white mustache, suspenders) beams across the yard.
Grandpa!
units.name: BEA

units.text: Where is my birthday girl?
units.name: OSWALDO

units.text: ^Where is my present?
units.name: BEA

units.text: Where is my birthday girl?
units.name: OSWALDO

units.text: The two speak over each other, gleeful, and collapse into laughter.
June sets down the tray and shakes her head.
Papa, you're early.
units.name: JUNE

units.text: I brought a surprise. Open it, Bea.
units.name: OSWALDO

units.text: Bea tears the paper.
Inside, a tiny wooden sign reading "BEA'S COOP."
Her eyes shine.
Grandpa, it's perfect.
units.name: BEA

units.text: I carved it myself. Terrible carpenter, but good heart.
units.name: OSWALDO

units.text: Great, now we're all going to cry.
units.name: THEO

units.text: He is already wiping his nose.
The gate clicks again.
MRS. PETRAKIS (70s, next-door neighbor, enormous sun hat, a pie held out like an offering) shuffles in.
I smelled cake from my kitchen. I brought apple.
units.name: MRS. PETRAKIS

units.text: June pulls out her phone to photograph the moment.
The hen returns, pecks at the cake, and nobody stops her.
Penelope, no! That's for the guests!
units.name: BEA

units.text: Penelope looks up, frosting on her beak.
Everyone laughs.
The afternoon goes golden.
